cost.note: translation is assemble + one symbolic execution per fence-delimited block, linear in the program for straight-line blocks

notes: The second leg of the C / RISC-V / BTOR2 triangle, and the pair that makes riscv a machine: T.py embeds the riscv interpreter's assembler verbatim, takes every frame start (the entry, and the instruction after each fence) as a block, executes the block symbolically as a DAG merged at joins by ite over pairwise-disjoint path conditions, and emits one transition per frame — pc over blocks with HALT and ERR absorbing, the registers ever written as bitvec-64 states, memory as one word-addressed array (bitvec 64 -> bitvec 64) with byte-granular loads and stores spliced through one word at a known constant address inside it and through two adjacent words otherwise (alignment never assumed), the data section as a write chain over the zero array, one btor2 input per constant havoc site, bad in the frame whose block reaches ebreak. Constant folding keeps `la`/`li` addresses concrete, so scalar cells cost one read or one read-modify-write. Refused: computed jumps, symbolic ecall codes or sites, a loop without a fence. obs identity; wit (lam_wit.py) re-runs the translator for its site map and renames \"<input id>\" -> \"<site>\" per frame; claim crosses at the full bound (frames align). Corpus: the seven c--riscv translations of the c--btor2 corpus plus six riscv vectors (data-section init, 32-bit ops, division by zero, frame-addressed reads). Pre-admission evidence: the composed square c -> riscv -> btor2 held on the 79 svcomp25-mini programs under random frame-addressed stimuli (square_riscv_btor2 record). No cert channel: btor2 has no certificate schema yet.
